questions.q: When Passepartout compares his new master to the people at Madame Tussaud's, what does he mean?
choices: Fogg seems as stiff and lifeless as a wax figure
Fogg looks like a famous man he once saw there
Fogg is as cheerful as the crowds who visit there
Fogg reminds him of a performer he worked with
questions.evidence: Madame Tussaud's "people," let it be said, are of wax

questions.q: About how old did Mr. Fogg appear to Passepartout?
choices: About thirty
About forty
About fifty-five
About twenty-five
questions.evidence: He appeared to be a man about forty years of age

questions.q: Why did Fogg, "so to speak," never rub against anybody?
choices: He was afraid of catching illnesses from crowds
He thought friction slows a person down
He disliked foreigners and avoided them
He had been told to by his doctor in Paris
questions.evidence: friction retards, he never rubbed against anybody

questions.q: Why did Passepartout leave his last master, young Lord Longferry?
choices: Lord Longferry refused to pay his wages for months
Lord Longferry moved away to live in Scotland
His mild complaint about the lord's wild nights was ill-received
Lord Longferry accused him of stealing a silver watch
questions.evidence: ventured a mild remonstrance on such conduct; which, being ill-received, he took his leave

questions.q: Passepartout "ventured a mild remonstrance" about his last master's behavior. What is a remonstrance?
choices: A loud cheer
A polite protest
A secret report
A long apology
questions.evidence: ventured a mild remonstrance on such conduct

questions.q: What did Passepartout find hung over the clock in his room?
choices: A card listing the daily routine of the house
A note from James Forster wishing him good luck
A painting of Mr. Fogg in his younger days
A key to the safe in Mr. Fogg's bedroom
questions.evidence: a programme of the daily routine of the house

questions.q: What did Passepartout notice was missing from the house in Saville Row?
choices: Gas lamps and fireplaces
A study, books and any weapons
Clocks or watches in any of the rooms
A kitchen and a dining room
questions.evidence: There was no study, nor were there books

questions.q: How does Passepartout feel about his new place by the end of the chapter?
choices: Worried that his strict master will dismiss him like James Forster
Joyful that he has found the quiet, regular master he wanted
Bored and already planning to look for a livelier household
Puzzled about where his strange master's fortune came from
questions.evidence: This is just what I wanted!
